headline: Highest risk is medium: ComfyUI can ingest files and run offline, but the paired awesome-list has no runnable surfaces, so interaction risks are limited and mostly indirect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default instruction bridge exists: agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b has no clipboard/stdin and only file-based model assets. Without a shared channel, agent_a cannot inject instructions into agent_b by default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies agent_a content into agent_b prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep agent_a as reference-only, not prompt input.
Disable any copy-paste workflow from agent_a into agent_b prompts.
Do not mount a shared workspace between the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches no data classes and has no I/O, while agent_b is offline by default and only handles local model assets. The pair does not show a shared workspace or outbound upload path, so leakage is not evident; uncertainty is low because both profiles lack a shared data channel.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is mounted containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is configured to upload prompts or files through the Comfy API, data exposure changes.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files off any shared directory.
Run agent_b in offline mode.
Separate OS users for the two agents.
Review Comfy API settings before enabling uploads.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or container mounts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a has no write or execution capabilities, and agent_b explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable write surface, there is no capability conflict pathway in the default profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b is replaced with a writable deployment, conflicts could emerge.
IF a separate orchestrator grants shared write access, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only with respect to shared repos.
Do not grant filesystem write permissions to either agent.
Avoid running multiple instances against the same mutable state.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a is a curated reference list, not an action-taking system, so its outputs are not authoritative operational facts. Agent_b can use workflows and Comfy API, but the pair lacks a documented direct pipeline from agent_a into agent_b, making cascading error possible only through manual reuse.
conditions: IF an operator treats agent_a recommendations as executable instructions for agent_b, errors can cascade.
IF agent_a content is pasted into agent_b workflows without verification, the pathway becomes active.
mitigations: Verify any agent_a recommendation before use in agent_b.
Use a checklist for workflow changes sourced from agent_a.
Keep agent_a outputs out of automated ComfyUI pipelines.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before workflow import.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: agent_a touches no regulated data classes, and agent_b's documented data classes are media/model artifacts rather than PHI or residency-sensitive records. With no cited residency, certification, or retention conflict, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into agent_b workflows, compliance analysis must be revisited.
IF a deployment adds retention or residency constraints not shown here, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document data-class boundaries for ComfyUI workflows.
Review retention settings before enabling any logging.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
